name: Concurrent exact-retry native admission with independent loopback effects
caller: The same optional Pi native Harness/GenerationTask/Faux/ToolTask/HTTP caller, with three simultaneous public admit() calls per Session: two distinct conversation requests plus one exact retry. A before-reserve barrier proves overlap before any reservation is committed. The prior serial caller/adapter and all freezes remain unchanged as rollback.
scale_bottleneck: Concurrent callers can race durable host reservation, stable native submit and host-link commits. An exact retry must return the same native submission without a second chain or effect; changed content must be refused and every committed active inventory stay <=2. This is concurrent callers within one owner, not concurrent SQLite owners.
stage0: Two reservations per Session held after durable effect intent/before transport; one remote-only authority withdrawal and one durable host cancel mark per Session; full-capacity refusal; force-kill native worker with no HTTP effect request yet.
stage1: Recover GET404 intents, remote POST403 and host pre-cancel refusal, exact original native abort/terminal reaping; admit one normal completion and one remote commit with deliberately held reply per Session. Cancel-mark the latter after independent commit and force-kill before acknowledgement.
stage2: Recover the two committed remote receipts via GET without another POST before resolving original native tasks. Admit two normal completions per Session and refuse overload; explicitly probe two exact duplicate POSTs and two changed-content conflicts against original recovered keys. Reap all host/native work, no tool/provider replay.
acceptance: Exact immutable request/native-chain/intent/receipt joins; separate SQLite integrity and full stopped-source/copied endpoint equality at all stages; 16 arrivals/12 host/4 overload, 12 native chains, 8 remote rows count1, 28 exact method/status/key effect attempts, 6 recovered reservations, 12 host and24 native task terminals, finalactive0; three observed native and three server PIDs with correct exits; fixed resource/time/output gates. Additional preregistered28public admission results:12admit/6exactduplicate/6changed-content-conflict/4overload;6rounds each with all3reserve arrivals before release, exact retry joins same native submission, only12native chains and8remote rows as before. Full native/database/authority/cancel/reopen checks remain required.
metrics: Report applicable disposition success and counts; effects and six normal completions per suite/controller/full CLI time; mixed terminal latency n12 p50/p95/p99; native and server sampled private bytes/OS peak working sets with gaps; observed HTTP request/response body bytes (including partial response observations, excluding headers)/request wall times, native SQLite and remote DB bytes, callbacks/flush cost; authentication and preparation/publication costs separately. No baseline or causal performance conclusion.
limits: One trusted Windows host, six finite three-caller admission rounds under one trusted owner, two native SQLite Sessions and one separately persisted local SQLite effect database. Official local Faux is not a real model; HTTP reaches only a free loopback tool endpoint. Fixture header/control endpoints are not tenant authentication. Exact finite identities and transactional unique-key rows do not establish general external exactly-once, atomic host/remote policy, concurrent-owner or arbitrary transport/cancellation races, arbitrary network or crash-log durability, server failure injection, real API/GPU/distributed/production or SLO/causal performance. Histories grow, reconciliation/reaping is explicit, intermediate callback revisions need not remain in SQLite history. Old H1/H2 failures/results and H3/H4 remain unchanged. The barrier controls before-reserve concurrency only. Remote authority changes and cancellation remain at the fixed held transport/reply boundaries from the prior caller, not arbitrary interleavings or a linearizability proof. No queue or runtime modification is introduced.
exit_condition: One separately reviewed/frozen complete suite only; preserve failures without rerun or threshold changes. Acceptance closes only this concurrent public admission/exact-retry slice in the existing native caller. No further standalone observer prerequisites; further work needs an actual runner or independently justified authority/cancellation intervention.
recovery_native_resume_gate: On each reopened paused Harness, first reconcile durable HTTP intents without resuming native work. Validate every original active request/submission/user identity and inspect the exact GenerationTask/ToolTask assistant/call/arguments/owner chain. Before any conversation-wide abort can resume the scheduler, mark both generation and tool task IDs for every cancelled or remote-denied recovered request using public Harness.abortTask; require the scheduler remains paused and all intended IDs are marked. Only then reconcile conversation abort/wait and resume. No private scheduler or direct native task mutation.
remote_identity_scope: Native conversation/submission/task/entry IDs remain exact positive safe integers. Session-local conversation IDs may repeat across the two SQLite Sessions. Durable remote identities therefore include stable service0/service1 scope; current authority is keyed by (scope, native conversation ID). Request keys retain exact native conversation and fixed per-service request IDs. A cross-scope receipt cannot acknowledge another intent. This trusted fixture namespace is not tenant authentication.
prefreeze_revision_note: No runtime/admission/transport semantics modified. New finite caller, overlap evidence and additional acceptance are declared before any implementation freeze, scientific reservation or native execution.
